summary: Iteration 3 testing: BYO LLM key + model dropdown, Company Overview rename + active toggle, two script types (line-by-line + personality), Windows easy setup. Backend pytest 53/53 pass (incl. new test_llm_config.py). Frontend Playwright covered login, LLM provider/model dropdowns + validate (Gemini=valid, OpenAI=quota-exceeded, sk-bad=invalid), Company Overview tab rename + KB Active/Disabled toggle, both script types save with correct type badge. Windows artifacts (start.bat + README Windows section) verified statically.

minor.issue: Some Gemini model names in the dropdown return quota-exceeded for the same key that succeeds with gemini-2.5-flash / gemini-3.5-flash (e.g. gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-2.5-pro). This appears provider-side (per-model quota), but several models in /api/llm/models do not exist publicly yet (e.g. gpt-5.4/5.5, gemini-3.x preview names) — UX risk: a user picking the default first model from a fresh Gemini dropdown will see 'quota exceeded' even with a perfectly valid key.

ui_bugs.issue: Provider-specific API key fields are sticky across provider switches: typing the Gemini key, then switching the Provider dropdown to OpenAI (without explicitly clearing) leaves data.gemini_api_key populated. Clicking Save with provider=anthropic and the visible llm-key empty persists the previously-typed Gemini key in the workspace. After my test the workspace had gemini_api_key set despite the input being blank at save time. Had to clear via PUT /api/settings/integrations. Expected: Save should only persist the *currently selected* provider's key, OR switching providers should not silently retain a typed key for the previous provider.

action_items: Fix sticky LLM key bug in Settings.IntegrationsTab: when the user changes the Provider dropdown, either clear the previously-typed `llm-key` field from form state, OR have Save only PUT the api_key field that matches the currently-selected provider. Right now the user can leak a custom key into the workspace by typing → validate → switch provider → save.

Review Gemini default model in /api/llm/models — the first option (`gemini-3.1-pro-preview`) returns quota-exceeded against a key that works fine on `gemini-2.5-flash`. Consider promoting a known-stable model to the top so the dropdown's default validates cleanly.
Consider rounding out OpenAI/Gemini model lists with currently-public names so users don't pick non-existent models by default.
critical_code_review_comments: BYO LLM key handling in Settings.IntegrationsTab.jsx: form state retains every provider's key independently — the Save handler PUTs the full data object, so prior typed keys remain. Either reset {openai/anthropic/gemini}_api_key on provider change, or scope Save to only the active provider's key.
Backend integrations.validate_llm_key correctly distinguishes Invalid vs quota-exceeded vs valid — good UX (matches spec).

GET /api/llm/models is unauthenticated-friendly and returns three lists keyed by provider; OK. Lists include several pre-release model names — confirm these resolve in your LLM provider abstraction or document them as 'coming soon'.
Frontend uses native <select> elements with data-testids for llm-provider/llm-model (good — easy to test via select_option).
Company Overview tab rename complete; kb-toggle endpoint (PUT /api/kb/{id}/toggle) works server-side and the UI reflects Active <-> Disabled state.
Script type badges (`Line-by-line` / `Personality`) render correctly in script cards; both selectable in Test Calls (script-type discriminator present in POST /api/scripts payload).
Windows start.bat exists at /app/start.bat and README has a 'Windows (10/11)' section referencing it — matches spec.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on tested flows (Login, LLM dropdowns+validate x3 outcomes, Company Overview rename+toggle, two script types save with badges) — 1 high-priority UI bug found re: sticky LLM key on Save

rca of the issue: Sticky LLM key bug RCA: IntegrationsTab keeps a single `data` object with separate fields data.openai_api_key / data.anthropic_api_key / data.gemini_api_key. The llm-key input is bound to whichever provider is currently selected in llm-provider. When you type a key for provider A, switch to B, type nothing (or another key), and Save, the PUT body still contains the unchanged data.{A}_api_key from before. Repro: (1) Settings → Integrations → set provider=gemini → paste any string in llm-key. (2) Switch provider to openai. (3) Clear llm-key (now bound to openai_api_key). (4) Click Save. (5) GET /api/settings/integrations shows gemini_api_key still set. Mitigation: on provider change, reset all three provider key fields except the currently-selected one to '' in form state; or make Save only send openai/anthropic/gemini_api_key for the currently active provider; or render three independent labelled inputs (one per provider) so user can see/clear each.
